title: An OpenCode orchestrator's wait is killed at 120 seconds, halfway through its chunk
foundBy: session agent, measuring how each agent CLI treats a 150-second command while tracing SAC-082
details:
The orchestrator's `wait` blocks for up to one chunk, 240 seconds by default. OpenCode 1.18.32 bounds a shell call at 120 seconds unless the model passes a larger timeout. Past the bound it kills the command and says `shell tool terminated command after exceeding timeout 120000 ms`.

This was measured on the host with a 150-second command. When the model passed no timeout, the command was killed at 120 seconds. When it passed one, the command ran to completion. An OpenCode orchestrator that calls `wait` plainly therefore fails every chunk that runs past two minutes. It most likely calls `wait` again, so the campaign still moves, but each such chunk costs a failed call and a turn step.

The Claude half of this was fixed in SAC-082 by raising the bound when the orchestrator is created. OpenCode's binary names `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, which may be the same lever. Codex was measured with no such bound. No smoke scenario runs an OpenCode orchestrator, so the replay tier cannot see this.

notes.text: The variable works. On the host, OpenCode 1.18.32 ran a 150-second command twice, and both calls passed no timeout. Unset, the command was killed at 120 seconds. With `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` it ran to completion. The fix can take the shape of SAC-082's, set when an OpenCode orchestrator is created.
